mainTopic: Consecrating only part of an animal: whether the holiness spreads to the whole animal, and what the partial holiness means in practice.
overview: A ברייתא discusses someone who says, 'The leg of this animal is an עולה.' According to רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה, only the leg becomes holy. The animal is sold to someone who needs an עולה, and only the money for the leg is holy. רבא explains that the buyer is someone who vowed an 'עולה בחייה', so the missing leg does not hurt his vow. According to רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון, the whole animal becomes an עולה. רב חסדא, רבא and רב ששת each say that רבי יהודה agrees when the limb is vital, but they define 'vital' differently. A statement of רבי seems to refute all three, and the גמרא answers by filling in missing words. רבא then asks whether the rule applies to a bird and to a limb consecrated only for its value; both questions end with תיקו. Finally, the גמרא asks about shearing or working an animal that is only partly holy, and the amud ends with a question about slaughtering a holy mother whose fetus is not holy.

steps.title: Consecrating a leg does not make the whole animal an עולה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from the word 'ממנו' (of it) that when someone consecrates one limb as an עולה, the whole animal does not become an עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: You might think that if someone says 'The leg of this animal is an עולה,' the whole animal becomes an עולה. So the פסוק says 'Anything of it that one gives to ה' shall be holy.' 'Of it' goes to ה', but not all of it.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא raises a case where a person consecrates just one leg of an animal as an עולה. It learns from the פסוק that only that part becomes holy, not the whole animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first suggests that holiness might spread from the leg to the whole animal. It rejects this from the word 'ממנו', which means 'part of it.' That word shows that the Torah allows a person to give just a part of an animal.

keyTerms.meaning: A burnt offering, burned completely on the מזבח
'You might think'; it opens a possibility that the ברייתא is about to reject
'The פסוק teaches'; it introduces a proof from a פסוק
'Of it,' meaning part of it

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
One might think that one who says: "The leg of this one is a burnt offering"
the whole of it should be a burnt offering?
The verse states:
"Anything of it that one gives to the Lord
shall be sacred"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:9

phrases.english: "Of it" to the Lord, and not all of it to the Lord.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: יָכוֹל הָאוֹמֵר ״רַגְלָהּ שֶׁל זוֹ עוֹלָה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Consecrating one limb as an עולה does not make the whole animal an עולה (learned from 'ממנו').

steps.title: The consecrated leg still does not become ordinary
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. Even though the whole animal is not an עולה, the leg itself cannot become plain חולין, because the פסוק says 'יהיה קדש'.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think the leg goes back to being ordinary. So the פסוק says 'shall be holy.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא blocks the opposite extreme. The leg is not simply let go as ordinary; it stays holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 showed that the holiness does not spread to the whole animal. Now someone might think the consecration does not work at all. The words 'יהיה קדש' teach that the part that was given really is holy.

keyTerms.meaning: Ordinary, non-holy things
'Go out to ordinary status,' meaning lose its holiness
'It shall be holy'

phrases.english: One might think it goes out to non-sacred status?
phrases.notes: 'It' means the leg that was given as an עולה.

phrases.english: The verse states: "Shall be sacred."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Balances step 1: not all of it is holy, but the part that was given is still holy.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The consecrated limb keeps its holiness and does not become חולין.

steps.title: The practical solution: sell the animal to someone who needs an עולה
steps.stepSummary: The animal is sold to a person who will bring it as an עולה. The money for the animal is ordinary, except for the money paid for the consecrated limb. This is the view of רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: So what do we do? The animal is sold to someone who needs an עולה. The money is ordinary, except for the money for the limb that was consecrated. These are the words of רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains what to do in practice, since only one leg of a live animal is holy. It ends by naming who holds this view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You cannot cut off a leg and offer it, so the whole animal goes to a buyer who will bring it all as an עולה. That way the holy leg ends up on the מזבח. The owner keeps the money for the rest of the animal, but the money for the leg's share is holy.

keyTerms.meaning: 'How so?' It asks how to carry out the rule in practice
For the needs of people bringing an עולה
Its money (the payment for the animal)
A limb

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה, only the leg is holy. The animal is sold for an עולה, and only the money for the leg is holy.

phrases.english: How is this?
It should be sold for the needs of burnt offerings,
phrases.notes: 'It' is now the whole animal, sold to someone who will offer all of it.

phrases.english: and its payment is non-sacred,
except for the payment for the limb in it.
These are the words of Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Puts steps 1 and 2 into practice and names who holds this view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The animal is sold for an עולה, and only the money for the consecrated limb is holy.

steps.title: The other view: consecrating a leg makes the whole animal an עולה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון disagree. They learn from 'יהיה קדש' that the whole animal becomes an עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון say: How do we know that if someone says 'The leg of this animal is an עולה,' the whole animal is an עולה? The פסוק says 'Anything of it that one gives to ה'.' When it then says 'shall be holy,' that comes to include the whole animal.
steps.whatsHappening: Here the second side of the מחלוקת speaks. They hold that the holiness spreads to the entire animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides use the same פסוק. For רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון, 'ממנו' describes giving only a part. Then 'יהיה קדש' comes to add that the whole animal becomes holy. So there is no need to sell it; the whole animal is simply brought as an עולה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'From where do we know?' It asks for a source
'To include'; a word in the פסוק adds more cases

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides use the same words 'יהיה קדש'. In step 2 they only keep the leg holy. Here they make the whole animal holy.

phrases.english: But Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Shimon say:
From where is it derived for one who says: "The leg of this one is a burnt offering,"
that all of it is a burnt offering?
As it is stated: "Anything of it that one gives to the Lord,"
when it says: "Shall be sacred,"
it is to include all of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Consecrating one limb as an עולה makes the entire animal an עולה.

steps.title: Challenge: the buyer would be bringing an animal missing a limb
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the view of רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה. How can the buyer use this animal for his own עולה, when one limb is not his?
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: The animal is sold for the needs of עולות. But then the buyer is bringing an animal that is missing a limb!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to step 3 and raises a problem with selling the animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The leg already belongs to the הקדש. So the buyer is really paying for, and offering, an animal without that leg. An עולה that is missing a limb seems unfit for his obligation.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But surely...'; it introduces a problem
Missing a limb

phrases.english: The Master said:
phrases.notes: He is quoting the ברייתא from step 3.

phrases.english: It should be sold for the needs of burnt offerings.
But he is bringing an animal lacking a limb!
phrases.notes: The leg was already holy, so the buyer's share is the animal without that leg.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: תִּמָּכֵר לְצׇרְכֵי עוֹלוֹת, וְהָא קָמַיְיתֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to step 3 and attacks how its sale can work.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that the animal is sold for the needs of עולות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The buyer's offering would really be an animal missing a limb, so it seems unfit for his own vow.

steps.title: Answer: the sale is to someone who vowed an 'עולה בחייה'
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the ברייתא means a buyer who vowed 'הרי עלי עולה בחייה'. His vow covers only the parts the animal's life depends on, so the missing leg does not hurt him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It is talking about someone who said 'I take upon myself an עולה with its life,' meaning the parts its life depends on.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge by narrowing who the buyer is. It is not just anyone who needs an עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This buyer only promised the parts the animal's life depends on. The leg is not one of those, so the leg that belongs to the הקדש does not take anything away from his vow. That way the sale in step 3 still works.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I take upon myself'; the wording of a vow
'With its life,' meaning the parts its life depends on

steps.whatToRemember: The sale in step 3 works because the buyer vowed an 'עולה בחייה'. His vow covers only the parts its life depends on, so the missing leg does not matter to him.

phrases.english: Rava says:
It is referring to one who says: "It is upon me to bring a burnt offering with its life."
phrases.notes: 'With its life' means the parts the animal's life depends on. A leg is not one of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: בְּאוֹמֵר ״הֲרֵי עָלַי עוֹלָה בְּחַיֶּיהָ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (who the buyer is)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The animal could be sold to anyone obligated in an עולה, but then it would be missing a limb.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is sold to someone who vowed an 'עולה בחייה', and the consecrated leg does not take away from that vow.

steps.title: Three views on when רבי יהודה agrees the whole animal becomes holy
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא, רבא and רב ששת each define the limb for which רבי יהודה admits that the holiness spreads to the whole animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: רבי יהודה admits that the whole animal becomes holy if a person dedicated a limb whose loss makes the animal a טרפה. רבא said: only a limb whose loss makes it a נבילה. רב ששת said: only a limb without which the animal dies.
steps.whatsHappening: Three אמוראים say that רבי יהודה does agree with רבי יוסי in one kind of case, but they disagree about which limb counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now רבי יהודה held that dedicating one limb does not make the whole animal an עולה. Now we learn there is an exception: a limb the animal cannot live without. רב חסדא sets the widest limit (a טרפה limb), רבא a narrower one (a נבילה limb), and רב ששת the narrowest (a limb without which the animal really dies).

keyTerms.meaning: Admits, agrees in this case
An animal with a deadly injury or defect, which may not be eaten
An animal treated like a carcass, as if already dead
Dies

steps.confusionAlert: None of these three say רבי יהודה changed his main view. They only say there is one exception: a limb the animal's life depends on.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
Rabbi Yehuda admits
phrases.notes: He means רבי יהודה admits that here the whole animal becomes an עולה, like רבי יוסי says.

phrases.english: regarding a limb that makes it a tereifa.
phrases.notes: Meaning a limb that, if it were missing, would make the animal a טרפה.

phrases.english: Rava said:
regarding a limb that makes it a neveilah.
And Rav Sheshet said:
regarding a limb without which it dies.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: מוֹדֶה רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the מחלוקת between רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי and defines when רבי יהודה admits the whole animal becomes holy.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה admits that dedicating a vital limb makes the whole animal holy. רב חסדא: a טרפה limb. רבא: a נבילה limb. רב ששת: a limb without which it dies.

steps.title: What is the difference between רב חסדא and רבא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical case separates רב חסדא from רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between רב חסדא and רבא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the practical difference between the first two views. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טרפה limb and a נבילה limb sound close. The גמרא wants to know in what real case the two views give different results.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them? (in practice)

phrases.aramaic: מַאי אִיכָּא בֵּין רַב חִסְדָּא לְרָבָא?
phrases.english: What is the difference between Rav Chisda and Rava?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אִיכָּא בֵּין רַב חִסְדָּא לְרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical difference between the first two opinions in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what practical case do רב חסדא and רבא disagree?

steps.title: They disagree whether a טרפה can survive
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא holds a טרפה cannot live, so a טרפה limb is vital. רבא holds a טרפה can live, so a טרפה limb is not vital enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is whether a טרפה can live. רב חסדא follows the view that a טרפה cannot live. רבא follows the view that a טרפה can live.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the two disagree on whether an animal that is a טרפה can keep living.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a טרפה cannot live (רב חסדא), then a limb whose loss makes it a טרפה is a limb its life depends on, so the whole animal becomes holy. If a טרפה can live (רבא), that limb is not vital, so you need a stronger limb, one whose loss makes it a נבילה.

keyTerms.meaning: A טרפה can survive (live on)
A טרפה cannot survive
He holds like the one who says

phrases.english: The difference between them is whether a tereifa can live.
Rav Chisda holds
like the one who says a tereifa cannot live,
and Rava holds
like the one who says a tereifa can live.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They disagree whether a טרפה can survive: רב חסדא says no, so a טרפה limb is vital; רבא says yes, so it is not.

steps.title: What is the difference between רבא and רב ששת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical case separates רבא from רב ששת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the difference between רבא and רב ששת?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks for the difference between the second and third views. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נבילה limb and a limb without which the animal dies seem almost the same. The גמרא wants a case where they split.

phrases.aramaic: וּמַאי אִיכָּא בֵּין רָבָא לְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת?
phrases.english: And what is the difference between Rava and Rav Sheshet?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי אִיכָּא בֵּין רָבָא לְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same kind of question as step 8, now for the second pair of opinions.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what practical case do רבא and רב ששת disagree?

steps.title: They disagree about רבי אלעזר's rule on a removed thigh
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says an animal whose thigh and its hollow were removed is a נבילה. רבא accepts this; רב ששת does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is the view of רבי אלעזר, who said: if the thigh and its hollow were removed, the animal is a נבילה. רבא holds like רבי אלעזר; רב ששת does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: רבא and רב ששת disagree about the case of an animal that lost its thigh and the hollow where the thigh sits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר says such an animal already counts as a נבילה, even while alive. For רבא, who follows him, the thigh is a 'נבילה limb', so dedicating it makes the whole animal holy. רב ששת does not follow רבי אלעזר, and anyway the animal does not die at once, so for him the holiness does not spread.

keyTerms.meaning: Thigh, the hind leg
Its hollow, the socket where the thigh sits
Was removed

steps.whatToRemember: The three views go from wide to narrow: רב חסדא (a טרפה limb), רבא (a נבילה limb, including the thigh, like רבי אלעזר), רב ששת (only a limb without which the animal really dies).

phrases.english: The difference between them is the view of Rabbi Elazar,
for Rabbi Elazar said:
If the thigh and its hollow were removed, it is a neveilah.
phrases.notes: So even while it is still alive, the animal already counts as a carcass.

phrases.english: Rava holds like Rabbi Elazar,

phrases.aramaic: רַב שֵׁשֶׁת לָא סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר.
phrases.english: Rav Sheshet does not hold like Rabbi Elazar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They disagree about רבי אלעזר's rule that an animal missing its thigh and hollow is a נבילה: רבא accepts it, רב ששת does not.

steps.title: A challenge from רבי: רבי יהודה never admitted
steps.stepSummary: רבי said רבי יהודה is right about a non-vital limb and רבי יוסי is right about a vital limb. This suggests that רבי יוסי argued with רבי יהודה even about a vital limb.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: רבי said, the words of רבי יהודה seem right for a limb the animal's life does not depend on, and the words of רבי יוסי seem right for a limb the animal's life does depend on. Doesn't this show that רבי יוסי argued with רבי יהודה even about a vital limb?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a statement of רבי that seems to contradict all three אמוראים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three אמוראים said רבי יהודה himself admits about a vital limb. But רבי had to 'split' the dispute, saying רבי יהודה is right only for a non-vital limb and רבי יוסי for a vital one. That suggests רבי יהודה himself said the holiness does not spread even for a vital limb, so he did not admit at all.

keyTerms.meaning: The words seem right (a ruling of which view to follow)
The animal's life depends on it, a vital limb
By implication, it follows from this
He argues with him

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'רבי' with no name is רבי יהודה הנשיא, who wrote the משנה. He is not the same person as רבי יהודה whose view is being discussed.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
Rabbi said:
phrases.notes: This is רבי יהודה הנשיא, not the רבי יהודה of the dispute.

phrases.english: The words of Rabbi Yehuda seem right
for a limb that the animal's life does not depend on,
and the words of Rabbi Yosei
for a limb that the animal's life depends on.

phrases.aramaic: לָאו מִכְּלָל דִּפְלִיג עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה?
phrases.english: Doesn't this imply that he argues with Rabbi Yehuda?
phrases.notes: He means רבי יוסי argued with רבי יהודה even about a vital limb, so רבי יהודה did not admit there.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: אָמַר רַבִּי: נִרְאִין דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the shared assumption of the three אמוראים in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim of רב חסדא, רבא and רב ששת that רבי יהודה admits about a vital limb.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי יהודה already admitted about a vital limb, רבי would not need to say that רבי יוסי is right there. Splitting the dispute implies that רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי argued even about a vital limb.

steps.title: The inference from רבי's words seems to refute all three אמוראים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out the challenge. Saying רבי יוסי is right about a vital limb implies that רבי יהודה disagreed with him there, which refutes everyone who said רבי יהודה agrees in that case.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that calling רבי יהודה right about a non-vital limb shows the two argued about that case. But calling רבי יוסי right about a vital limb must also mean they argued about that case. That refutes all of the אמוראים who said רבי יהודה agrees there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the attack from step 12. It reads רבי's words to mean that רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי argued about a vital limb too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You only need to say 'רבי יוסי is right' about a case if someone disagreed with him there, and that someone is רבי יהודה. But רב חסדא, רבא and רב ששת all built their views on the idea that רבי יהודה agrees about a vital limb. So all three seem to be refuted at once.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense (granted); this part is fine, but the next part is a problem
By implication; what we learn from how something is said
A limb the animal's life depends on (a vital limb)
A strong refutation

phrases.english: It makes sense: 'The words of רבי יהודה appear correct
regarding a thing on which life does not depend,'
which implies that he disagrees with רבי יוסי there.
But 'The words of רבי יוסי appear correct
regarding a thing on which life depends':

phrases.aramaic: לָאו מִכְּלָל דִּפְלִיג עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה?
phrases.english: doesn't that imply that he disagrees with רבי יהודה there too?
And that is a refutation of all of them!
phrases.notes: 'All of them' means רב חסדא, רבא and רב ששת. Each of them said רבי יהודה agrees when the limb is vital.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the challenge started in step 12 by spelling out the inference and its result.
steps.kashyaTarget: The shared assumption of רב חסדא, רבא and רב ששת that רבי יהודה agrees about a vital limb
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Calling רבי יוסי 'right' about a vital limb only makes sense if רבי יהודה disagreed with him there.

steps.title: The teaching is missing words: רבי יהודה agrees about a vital limb
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי's statement is missing words. Correctly read, it says that רבי יהודה himself accepts רבי יוסי's view about a vital limb.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, words are missing, and this is what it means: רבי יהודה agrees with רבי יוסי about a limb the animal's life depends on. רבי יהודה only disagreed about a limb the animal's life does not depend on. About a vital limb, he agrees with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rescues the three אמוראים by filling in missing words in רבי's statement. Read this way, רבי יהודה agrees with רבי יוסי about a vital limb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The added words 'to רבי יהודה' change the meaning completely. 'רבי יוסי is right' no longer means רבי יהודה lost an argument about a vital limb. Now it means רבי יהודה himself accepts רבי יוסי's view there. So the argument is only about a non-vital limb, and the אמוראים are safe.

keyTerms.meaning: Words are missing from the teaching, and the גמרא fills them in
Disagreed
Agrees

steps.whatToRemember: Final picture: רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי argue only about a non-vital limb. About a vital limb, both agree that the whole animal becomes holy.
steps.confusionAlert: 'נראין דברי רבי יוסי לרבי יהודה' does not mean רבי decided against רבי יהודה. It means רבי יהודה himself agrees with רבי יוסי in this case.

phrases.english: No, words are missing from it
and this is what it teaches:

phrases.aramaic: נִרְאִין דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: The words of רבי יוסי appear correct to רבי יהודה
regarding a thing on which life depends,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאַף רַבִּי יְהוּדָה לֹא נֶחְלַק עָלָיו
phrases.english: for even רבי יהודה did not disagree with him

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא בְּדָבָר שֶׁאֵין הַנְּשָׁמָה תְּלוּיָה בּוֹ,
phrases.english: except regarding a thing on which life does not depend,
but regarding a thing on which life depends
he agrees with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the refutation in step 13 by reading רבי's statement differently.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Fixing the wording (חסורי מיחסרא): missing words are filled in
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי's words meant that רבי יוסי was right against רבי יהודה, even about a vital limb.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי's words mean that רבי יהודה agrees with רבי יוסי about a vital limb. They disagree only about a non-vital limb.

steps.title: Does the rule apply to a bird? Unresolved
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks whether רבי יוסי's rule, that consecrating one limb makes the whole animal holy, also applies to a bird. The question stays unresolved (תיקו).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked: what is the law for a bird? The Torah says 'animal', and a bird is not an 'animal'. Or perhaps the Torah says 'offering', and a bird is also an 'offering'. The question stays open.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about how far רבי יוסי's rule reaches. רבא asks whether it covers birds. No answer is found.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule comes from a פסוק that uses two words, 'animal' and 'offering'. If the key word is 'animal', a bird is left out. If the key word is 'offering', a bird is included, since birds can also be brought as offerings. The גמרא cannot decide which word matters, so it ends with תיקו.

keyTerms.meaning: Asks a question the גמרא really wants answered
Bird
Animal (from cattle, sheep or goats)
Offering
Let it stand; the question stays unresolved

phrases.english: רבא asked: With a bird, what is the law?
The Torah said 'animal',
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:9

phrases.english: and this is not an 'animal',
or perhaps the Torah said 'offering',
and this is also an 'offering'?
Let it stand unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the argument between רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי is settled, the גמרא asks how far רבי יוסי's rule goes.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the rule that one consecrated limb makes the whole animal holy also applies to a bird.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: None; the question ends with תיקו.

steps.title: A limb consecrated only for its value: does the whole animal become holy?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks about someone who consecrates one limb only for its money value. Does the whole animal then gain holiness of its body? That would need two steps of 'since' (מגו), and the question is whether we allow two.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked: if someone consecrated a limb for its value, does body-holiness come upon it? Do we say that since value-holiness came upon it, body-holiness comes too, and since he consecrated one limb, he consecrated the whole animal? Or perhaps we say one 'since' but not two?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks a second question about רבי יוסי's rule. The גמרא lays out both sides; the next step tries to answer it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To make the whole animal holy in its body, we need two jumps. First, from value-holiness to body-holiness. Second, from one limb to the whole animal. Each jump alone might work, but the question is whether we can make both together. That is the idea of 'one מגו but not two'.

keyTerms.meaning: Consecrated something for its money value, to be sold and the money used for the Temple
Holiness of value; only the item's worth is holy
Holiness of the body; the item itself is holy, ready for the altar
'Since', a step of reasoning: since this is true, that follows too
Limb

steps.confusionAlert: There are two separate 'since' steps here: value-holiness leading to body-holiness, and one limb leading to the whole animal. Don't mix them into one step.

phrases.english: רבא asked: If he consecrated a limb for its value,
what is the law: does body-holiness come upon it?
phrases.notes: 'It' here means the animal. The question is whether the whole animal becomes holy for the altar.

phrases.aramaic: מִי אָמַר: כֵּיוָן דְּנָחֲתָא לֵיהּ קְדוּשַּׁת דָּמִים
phrases.english: Do we say: since value-holiness came upon it,
body-holiness also comes upon it,
and since he consecrated one limb,
he consecrated all of it,
or perhaps we say one 'since',
but we do not say two 'since's?
phrases.notes: The two 'since's are the two jumps above: from value to body, and from one limb to the whole animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second question from רבא about how far רבי יוסי's rule reaches, this time about the kind of holiness.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether consecrating one limb for its value makes the whole animal holy in its body, which would require two steps of מגו.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: None; a proof is tried in step 17, rejected in step 18, and the question ends with תיקו.

steps.title: Trying to answer רבא's question from his own ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests answering רבא's question with רבא's own rule: if someone consecrates a male animal for its money value, it gets holiness of its body.
steps.simpleTranslation: Answer it from רבא's own words! רבא said: if a person consecrated a male animal for its money value, it becomes holy with holiness of its body.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer רבא's question (Step 16) by quoting another ruling of רבא himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא ruled that a male animal that can be brought as a קרבן becomes fully holy in body, even if the owner meant only its money value. So the same should happen here: money-value holiness should become holiness of the body.

keyTerms.meaning: Resolve it, answer the question
From his own (statement)
For its money value
Holiness of the body itself, so the animal must be offered

phrases.english: Resolve it from his own statement,
phrases.notes: "His own" means רבא's, the same רבא who asked the question.

phrases.english: for didn't רבא say:
If one consecrated a male for its value,
it is holy with holiness of its body!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attempts to resolve the question raised in Step 16.
steps.raayaObject: That money-value holiness can turn into holiness of the body in the one-limb case.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's own ruling: הקדיש זכר לדמיו קדוש קדושת הגוף.

steps.title: Rejecting the proof: one step versus two
steps.stepSummary: The proof fails. In רבא's ruling the whole animal was consecrated, so only one step is needed. Here only one limb was consecrated, so two steps are needed. The question stays open.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, he consecrated the whole animal. Here, he consecrated only one limb. So what is the law? It stays unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רבא's ruling is a different case, and then leaves the question unanswered (תיקו).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Consecrating the whole animal for money only needs one jump: money-holiness becomes body-holiness. With one limb there are two jumps: from the limb to the whole animal, and from money-holiness to body-holiness. רבא's ruling proves only the single jump.

keyTerms.meaning: A limb of the animal
Let the question stand; it stays unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: One 'since' (מגו) is accepted, but whether we allow two in a row is left unresolved: תיקו.

phrases.english: There, he consecrated all of it;
here, he consecrated one limb,
what is the law? Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof offered in Step 17 and closes רבא's question with תיקו.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from רבא's ruling about a male consecrated for its value.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That case needs only one expansion (money to body); the one-limb case needs two (limb to whole, money to body).
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The question of two expansions stays unresolved.

steps.title: אביי asks about shearing an animal with one consecrated limb
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רבא: if someone consecrated only one limb of an animal, is it forbidden to shear its wool?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי asked רבא: if someone consecrated one limb, what is the law about shearing it?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. אביי asks whether the ban on shearing a holy animal applies when only one limb is holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יהודה, holiness of one limb does not spread to the whole animal. So the animal is partly holy and partly ordinary. The question is whether partial holiness is enough to forbid shearing.

keyTerms.meaning: Shearing the wool
What is the law?

phrases.english: אביי asked רבא:
phrases.notes: The name אביי is in square brackets, so it belongs to the corrected wording. Some versions just say someone asked רבא.

phrases.english: If one consecrated one limb,
what is the law about shearing?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about a one-limb consecration, this time about shearing.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether an animal with only one consecrated limb is forbidden in shearing.

steps.title: רבא answers from a co-owned בכור
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers from a ברייתא: the פסוק forbids shearing 'your' בכור, so a בכור you share with others may be sheared. Here too the animal is shared, so shearing should be allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can answer it from a ברייתא: "Do not shear the firstborn of your flock." But you may shear one that belongs to you and to others.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers אביי by comparing his case to a בכור that is co-owned with others.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'your' in the פסוק teaches that the shearing ban applies only when the animal is fully yours. An animal with one holy limb is like a partnership between the הקדש and the owner, so the ban should not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: A firstborn animal, which is holy from birth
Do not shear
Belonging to others, here meaning partners who are not Jewish

phrases.english: You can resolve it from what was taught in a ברייתא:
"Nor shear the firstborn of your flock,"
phrases.notes: דברים 15:19

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אַתָּה גּוֹזֵז בְּשֶׁלְּךָ וְשֶׁל אֲחֵרִים.
phrases.english: but you may shear one that is yours and others'.
phrases.notes: The "others" are non-Jewish partners. Their share of a בכור does not become holy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's question from Step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Shearing should be allowed, just as a co-owned בכור may be sheared.

steps.title: Rejection: the co-owned בכור has no holiness at all
steps.stepSummary: The comparison fails. A co-owned בכור never received holiness at all, but here holiness did come onto the animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, no holiness came onto the animal at all. Here, holiness did come onto it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back: the בכור case is not like a consecrated limb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור with a non-Jewish partner is not holy at all, so of course it may be sheared. Here a real part of the animal is holy, so shearing may still be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Holiness came down on it, took effect
At all

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם, לָא נָחֲתָא לֵיהּ קְדוּשָּׁה כְּלָל;
phrases.english: There, holiness did not come down on it at all;
here, holiness did come down on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם לָא נָחֲתָא לֵיהּ קְדוּשָּׁה כְּלָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from the co-owned בכור in Step 20.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison between a co-owned בכור and an animal with one consecrated limb.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The co-owned בכור has no holiness at all; the one-limb animal is partly holy.

steps.title: Another version of the rejection: power to consecrate
steps.stepSummary: A second version of the rejection: in the בכור case the owner has no power to consecrate the animal, but here he does have power to consecrate the limb.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another version: There, it is not in his power to make it holy. Here, it is in his power to make it holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second way of saying why the בכור case is different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This version looks at the owner's power. A firstborn becomes holy by itself at birth, and a partner who is not Jewish blocks that, so the owner cannot make it holy. Here the owner chose to consecrate the limb and was able to, so the holiness is real and may forbid shearing.

keyTerms.meaning: Another version of the same discussion
It is in his power to consecrate it

steps.whatToRemember: Both versions agree that the co-owned בכור does not prove that one consecrated limb may be sheared. They only differ in how they explain the difference.

phrases.english: Another version:
There, it is not in his power to consecrate it;
here, it is in his power to consecrate it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of the rejection in Step 21.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The same proof from the co-owned בכור.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In the בכור case the owner has no power to consecrate; here he does, so the holiness truly takes effect.

steps.title: If only the skin is consecrated, may the animal be worked?
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רבא whether an animal whose skin alone was consecrated may be used for labor.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי asked רבא: If someone consecrated only the skin of an animal, may it be used for work?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי opens a new question about partial consecration. This time it is the skin, and the question is about doing work with the animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the skin is holy, not the animal's body. But working the animal can damage or thin its skin, and that lowers the value of the holy part. So the question is whether the holy skin makes it forbidden to work the whole animal.

keyTerms.meaning: He consecrated (made something holy, belonging to the בית המקדש)
Its skin (the animal's hide)
Labor: using the animal for work, like plowing or carrying loads

phrases.english: Abaye asked Rava:
If he consecrated its skin, what is the law regarding labor?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new question in the same series about partial consecration, moving from a consecrated limb and shearing to a consecrated skin and labor.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does consecrating only the skin forbid using the animal for labor?

steps.title: A ברייתא: a holy fetus forbids work but not shearing
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a ברייתא: if only the fetus is made an עולה, the mother may be sheared but not worked, because work weakens the fetus.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If someone says 'What is inside this animal's womb is an עולה,' the mother may be sheared but may not be worked, because work weakens the fetus inside her.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers from a ברייתא about a case where only part of the animal is holy, in this case the fetus.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא the mother herself is not holy, yet working her is forbidden because work hurts the holy fetus. The same should hold for a holy skin: working the animal harms the skin, so work should be forbidden. Shearing is allowed because it does not hurt the fetus.

keyTerms.meaning: Burnt offering, burned completely on the מזבח
Shearing (cutting the wool)
Weakening, making thinner or weaker
Fetus (the unborn animal)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
One who says, 'What is in the womb of this one is a burnt offering' —
she is permitted to be shorn, but forbidden for labor,
because of the weakening of the fetus inside her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23 by comparing it to a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Labor is forbidden, just as with a consecrated fetus, because labor harms the holy part.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא about consecrating the fetus as an עולה

steps.title: That ban is only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the ברייתא's ban on labor is only מדרבנן, so it does not answer his question about Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: When the ברייתא teaches that she is forbidden for labor, that is only a rabbinic law.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רבא's proof. The ברייתא's ban is a rule of the חכמים, and he wanted to know what the Torah itself says.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי was asking whether labor is forbidden מדאורייתא. A rabbinic ban in the ברייתא cannot prove a Torah-level ban, so the proof does not settle his question.

keyTerms.meaning: By rabbinic law (a rule made by the חכמים, not written in the Torah)
It teaches (what the ברייתא says)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think אביי is saying labor is fully allowed. He agrees it is forbidden. He is only saying the ban comes from the חכמים, so it cannot answer a question about Torah law.

phrases.english: He said to him:
When it teaches 'forbidden for labor,' that is by rabbinic law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 24.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof only shows a rabbinic ban, not a Torah ban.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The question was about Torah law, and the ברייתא's ban is only מדרבנן.

steps.title: Then shearing should be banned too
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges: if the ban is rabbinic, the חכמים should have forbidden shearing as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, even shearing should also be forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks אביי's explanation. If the חכמים added a ban, why did they ban only work and not shearing?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ban is a rabbinic safeguard and not about real harm, we would expect the חכמים to forbid every kind of benefit from the mother, shearing included. The fact that the ברייתא allows shearing seems to weaken אביי's claim.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (if what you said is true)
It should be forbidden

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי, אֲפִילּוּ בְּגִיזָּה נָמֵי תִּיתְּסַר!
phrases.english: If so, even shearing should also be forbidden!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי אֲפִילּוּ בְּגִיזָּה נָמֵי תִּיתְּסַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's claim in step 25 that the ban is rabbinic.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that the ban on labor is only מדרבנן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A rabbinic ban should also cover shearing, but the ברייתא permits shearing.

steps.title: Work weakens the animal, shearing does not
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers: the חכמים banned labor because it weakens the animal, and did not ban shearing because it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: With labor, which weakens the animal, the חכמים made a decree. With shearing, the חכמים did not make a decree.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends his position. The חכמים only made their ban where there is a reason for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rabbinic decree still needs a reason. Work weakens the mother and so harms the fetus, which gave the חכמים a reason to ban it. Shearing does no such harm, so they had no reason to ban it. The question about a consecrated skin and Torah law is left without a proof.

keyTerms.meaning: The חכמים made a decree (a protective ban)
That weakens (makes the animal thinner or weaker)

steps.whatToRemember: The ban on working an animal whose fetus is holy is only מדרבנן. It applies to work, which weakens the animal, and not to shearing, which does not. So אביי's question about a consecrated skin is not answered by this ברייתא.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Labor, which weakens — the Sages decreed against it;
shearing — the Sages did not decree against it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction based on the reason behind the decree
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A rabbinic ban should cover every use of the mother, shearing included.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חכמים banned only labor, because it weakens the animal. Shearing causes no harm, so they left it permitted.

steps.title: A שלמים with a non-holy fetus, slaughtered in the עזרה
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רב יוסף: if a pregnant animal is a שלמים but its fetus is חולין, and it is slaughtered inside the עזרה, what is the law?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי asked רב יוסף: If the mother is a שלמים and her fetus is not holy, and he slaughtered her inside the עזרה, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי opens a new question. The mother is holy and is slaughtered in the right place, but the fetus inside her is not holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is forbidden to slaughter חולין in the עזרה. When the holy mother is slaughtered there, the non-holy fetus is in effect slaughtered there too. The question is whether this counts as slaughtering חולין in the עזרה.

keyTerms.meaning: Peace offering
Her offspring (here, the fetus still inside her)
Non-holy, ordinary (not consecrated)
Inside (in the עזרה, the Temple courtyard)

phrases.english: Abaye asked Rav Yosef:
If she is a peace offering and her offspring is non-sacred,
and he slaughtered her inside, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new question on a new topic: whether slaughtering a holy animal carrying a non-holy fetus counts as חולין בעזרה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does slaughtering a שלמים in the עזרה while it carries a non-holy fetus count as slaughtering חולין in the עזרה?

steps.title: Offspring that only become holy at birth
steps.stepSummary: אביי adds a second case: according to the view that offspring of קדשים become holy only at birth, is the unborn fetus considered חולין בעזרה?
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says that offspring of קדשים become holy only when they are born, is this considered חולין in the עזרה, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי continues his question with a second way the fetus could be non-holy. Here the mother became pregnant after she was made holy, but by this view the fetus is not holy yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By this view the fetus has no holiness until it is born, so at the time of slaughter it is still חולין. The question is whether the ban on חולין בעזרה applies to it, or whether it does not apply because the fetus was not slaughtered on its own.

keyTerms.meaning: Offspring of holy animals
When they come into being (at birth)
Non-holy animals slaughtered in the Temple courtyard, which is forbidden
According to the one who says

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two cases. In step 28 the owner left the fetus out on purpose. Here the fetus is not holy only because, by this view, holiness starts at birth.

phrases.english: According to the one who says
offspring of sacrificial animals become holy when they come into being,
phrases.notes: He means at birth. Until then, the fetus inside is not yet holy.

phrases.aramaic: מִי הָוֵי חוּלִּין בַּעֲזָרָה אוֹ לָא?
phrases.english: is it considered non-sacred in the courtyard, or not?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַאן דְּאָמַר וַלְדֵי קָדָשִׁים בַּהֲוָיָיתָן הֵן קְדוֹשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands step 28's question to a second case in which the fetus is not holy.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: If offspring become holy only at birth, does slaughtering the pregnant mother in the עזרה count as slaughtering חולין in the עזרה?
